steps.label: What it is
steps.why: The two halves of the cerebrum work on different things, so a wide bridge of fibres is needed to keep them in step.
common_mistakes: Placing it between the cerebrum and the cerebellum. It joins the two cerebral hemispheres.
Calling it grey matter. It is a bundle of myelinated fibres.
steps.memory_tip: The bridge between the left and right halves of the cerebrum.

steps.label: What it does
steps.why: Because it carries traffic both ways, what one hemisphere learns the other can use.
common_mistakes: Writing that it controls movement. It coordinates the two hemispheres.
steps.memory_tip: It keeps the two halves working together.

lines.text: It coordinates the two cerebral hemispheres

insider_note: Say what it JOINS and what it DOES. An answer that only says 'a band of fibres in the brain' earns one mark of two.
